title: Bounded fibres and the maximum-degree open of an affine etale atlas
statement: Work over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ with schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum] and algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Give spaces the atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. For morphisms of spaces, separated means that the representable diagonal is a closed immersion on every scheme test [def-weil-closed-immersion]; quasi-compact means that inverse images of quasi-compact opens are quasi-compact; quasi-separated means that the diagonal is quasi-compact. Locally of finite type and locally of finite presentation are tested on etale scheme charts [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Finite type means quasi-compact and locally of finite type; finite presentation means quasi-compact, quasi-separated, and locally of finite presentation. Proper means separated, of finite type, and universally closed, where universally closed means closed on underlying spaces after every algebraic-space base change (agreeing with the scheme convention [def-weil-proper-morphism]). Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $X$ an algebraic space separated and of finite type over $B=\operatorname{Spec}A$, and $f:W\to X$ a representable surjective etale morphism with $W$ affine [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Then $W\to B$ is of finite type, and there is an integer $b\geq0$ bounding the number of points of every geometric fibre of $f$. Here a geometric fibre means $W\times_X\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ for an algebraically closed field $\Omega$ [def-weil-field] and a map $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$. If $X$ is nonempty, there is a least such bound $d\geq1$, and the set $U$ of points where this number is $d$ is a nonempty open subspace [def-weil-open-immersion]. The morphism $W\times_XU\to U$ is finite etale of constant degree $d$, meaning that on every etale scheme test its direct-image algebra is finite locally free of rank $d$. For the reduced closed subspace $T$ with support $|X|\setminus U$ [lem-sfb-space-reduced-closed-support], the scheme $W_T=W\times_XT$ is affine, $W_T\to T$ is representable surjective etale, and every geometric fibre has fewer than $d$ points. If $X$ is empty, $W$ is empty and $b=0$ is permitted.

source.place: Tag 03JX (lemma-bounded-fibres), implication (eta) => (delta), and Tag 07S8 (lemma-quasi-compact-reasonable-stratification), maximum-degree stratum; specialization used in spaces-cohomology.tex Tag 089J (lemma-weak-chow), first paragraph.

proof.text: The chartwise definition of local finite type for $X\to B$, applied to the etale source chart $f:W\to X$ and the identity chart of $B$, says that the scheme morphism $W\to B$ is locally of finite type. Since $W$ and $B$ are affine, the morphism $W\to B$ is affine by the lemma on morphisms between affine schemes. Thus $W\to B$ is quasi-compact by affine-morphism permanence, and hence of finite type. The affine schemes $W$ and $B$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Also $B\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is separated by the affine-source separation lemma. Composing it with the given separated $X\to B$ shows that $X$ is absolutely separated. Its absolute diagonal is therefore a closed immersion on scheme tests, hence affine by the affine characterization of a closed immersion, hence quasi-compact by affine-morphism permanence. Thus $X$ is quasi-separated in the absolute sense required below.

source.place: Tag 089J (lemma-weak-chow), first paragraph and its finite-type observation; separation uses spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 03KQ (lemma-composition-separated).

proof.text: The space quasi-compactness permanence lemma applies to $W\to X$, since $W$ is quasi-compact and $X$ is quasi-separated; hence $f$ is quasi-compact. To check its separatedness, first the scheme map $W\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is separated by affine-source separation. For any scheme map $H\to W\times_XW$, the scheme test of $\Delta_f$ is canonically $W\times_{W\times_{\mathbf Z}W}H\to H$: an equal pair of maps into $W$ has the same image in $X$. This is the base change of the closed absolute diagonal of $W$, so is a closed immersion. This verifies separatedness of $f$ without any separatedness assumption on a test scheme. The schemes and pullbacks in this computation exist by the scheme-test representability lemma.

Apply the quasi-compact etale-chart fibre-bound lemma to the quasi-separated space $X$ and the affine, hence quasi-compact, scheme $W$. It gives a nonnegative bound $b$ and finite discrete geometric fibres. If $X$ is empty, the map from $W$ forces $W$ empty and $b=0$ works. Assume henceforth $X$ nonempty. Surjectivity gives a nonempty geometric fibre over every geometric point: this also follows by the scheme-test surjectivity criterion and base change. Choose the least natural bound $d$ among the bounds bounded by $b$. Then $d\geq1$. If no fibre had $d$ points, all natural fibre cardinalities would be at most $d-1$, contradicting minimality. Thus the maximum $d$ is attained.

source.place: Tag 089J (lemma-weak-chow), first paragraph, minimal choice of d; decent-spaces.tex Tags 03JX (lemma-bounded-fibres) and 03JT (lemma-U-universally-bounded).

proof.text: Use the closed-degree-loci lemma for the quasi-compact separated etale morphism $f$ with the bound $d$. It says that $D_{d-1}=\{x:n(x)\leq d-1\}$ is closed. Its complement is exactly the locus $U=\{x:n(x)=d\}$, since all cardinalities are at most $d$, and it is nonempty by the preceding step. For completeness it has an open subspace structure: take the reduced closed subspace supported on $D_{d-1}$, and define its complementary subfunctor by requiring a scheme-source map to avoid that support. On every scheme test this is the complementary open of the pulled-back closed immersion, with its open subscheme structure. The sheaf condition is inherited by this local restriction, so this is a representable open subfunctor, hence an open algebraic subspace. This construction concerns an open complement and does not assert that a map with image in a closed subset factors through its reduced structure.

source.place: Tag 07S8 (lemma-quasi-compact-reasonable-stratification), closed degree filtration; spaces-properties.tex Tag 03IQ (lemma-reduced-closed-subspace).

proof.text: Let $V\to U$ be any scheme test, and put $E=W\times_XV$. The scheme-test lemma makes $E$ a scheme and $h:E\to V$ etale. Its geometric fibres are precisely those of $f$ over the composite geometric points into $X$, hence all have $d$ points. For $v\in V$, the etale fibre description writes $E_v$ as a disjoint union of spectra of finite separable extensions $L_j/\kappa(v)$. Each $L_j\otimes_{\kappa(v)}\Omega$ over an algebraic closure is a product of $[L_j:\kappa(v)]$ copies of $\Omega$, by the separable tensor lemma. Consequently there can be only finitely many $j$, since the geometric fibre has $d$ points. The fibre is affine by finite-disjoint-union affineness, and its coordinate algebra is $\prod_jL_j$, of dimension $\sum_j[L_j:\kappa(v)]=d$. This also shows directly that the geometric point count is unchanged under algebraically closed field extension: each split field factor stays one factor. Thus the point count and the finite fibre degree used by scheme stratification agree, including fibres over nonclosed points.

source.place: Tag 02GL (lemma-etale-over-field), fibre description; decent-spaces.tex Tag 07S8 (lemma-quasi-compact-reasonable-stratification), passage to a scheme test.

proof.text: The scheme map $h$ is flat and locally of finite presentation by the definition of etale, and is locally quasi-finite because etale implies unramified and the unramified-quasi-finite lemma applies. It is separated: a scheme test of its diagonal is a scheme test of $\Delta_f$, already proved closed. The preceding step supplies finite fibre degrees bounded by $d$. Apply the scheme bounded stratification theorem with bound $d$. Testing its universal property on each residue-field point identifies its degree-$r$ stratum with the points of fibre degree $r$. Every point of $V$ has degree $d$, so its degree-$d$ stratum is all of $V$. Apply that universal property again, now to $\mathrm{id}_V$, to conclude that $h:E\to V$ is finite locally free of degree $d$. Since it is etale, it is finite etale. This argument applies to every scheme test of $U$ and also when $V$ is empty.

source.place: Tag 07S8 (lemma-quasi-compact-reasonable-stratification), scheme-test argument, using more-morphisms.tex Tag 07RY (lemma-stratify-flat-fp-lqf-universally-bounded).

proof.text: For the sheaf-algebra meaning of the degree assertion, apply finite-flat pushforward to $h$ and the rank-one module $\mathcal O_E$. Its hypotheses are exactly the finiteness, flatness and local finite presentation just established. This gives $h_*\mathcal O_E$ finite locally free. The finite-flat rank lemma identifies its rank at $v$ with $\dim_{\kappa(v)}\Gamma(E_v,\mathcal O_{E_v})$, which is $d$ by the fibre calculation. Thus the direct-image algebra on every etale scheme test is finite locally free of rank $d$, as the statement requires.

source.place: Tag 02KB (lemma-finite-flat) and Tag 04MH (lemma-finite-locally-free), rank of the direct-image algebra.

proof.text: Let $T\hookrightarrow X$ be the reduced closed subspace with support $|X|\setminus U$. The reduced-support lemma, tested on the scheme $W\to X$, says that $W_T\to W$ is a closed immersion of schemes. Since $W$ is affine, the affine characterization of closed immersions writes $W_T=\operatorname{Spec}(C/I)$ when $W=\operatorname{Spec}C$; hence $W_T$ is affine. Base change of $f$ is representable surjective etale by the scheme-test permanence lemma. For a geometric point $\bar t$ of $T$, associativity of the sheaf fibre product identifies $(W_T)_{\bar t}$ with $W_{\bar t\to X}$. Its point in $X$ lies in the complement of $U$, so the already established natural cardinality is at most $d-1$, and is therefore less than $d$. When $d=1$, surjectivity forces $T$ empty, which is allowed. This completes all clauses.
